title: Twelve Smithion mass-ratio predictions and the dark-to-baryonic abundance from Fold geometry
description:
Read the full mathematical paper (PDF)

Twelve exact Smithion mass-ratio predictions, a neutral lightest relic class and dark-to-baryonic abundance 27/5 from Fold geometry.

Maria Smith derives four penta/hepta cubics from the complete prime-sector ladder and the existing coloured product p/[p(2p^d−1)−1]. The generated down/up cover depths are 7, 10, 9 and 12. Complete enumeration of the 1,024-cell grid and sixty exact halvings produce all twelve root brackets. The paper gives every endpoint in a compact integer table and the exact formula for all mass-ratio intervals.

The complete neutral sector fibres and unique least roots supply the lightest relic class in the source sector/generation construction. Generator volume 27 and its least binary cover 32 give baryonic and dark shares 5/32 and 27/32, dark/baryon 27/5 and matter/baryon 32/5. Generated lepton preimages and mode separations give flavour weights 1/32, 5/96 and 5/24, hence 3:5:20.

The original Planck comparison passes: 27/5 lies inside [238/45, 1210/223], and 27/5 times the released baryonic central density equals 0.12096 inside [0.119, 0.121]. The complete SPARC galaxy record, three null lepton-flavour search limits and original Smithion mass-measurement status are retained alongside the predictions.

All mathematics, intermediate counts, full candidate classifications and observational comparisons are in the paper. Native Lean 4 proofs, original pinned V3 code, exact arithmetic and source-bound verification receipts accompany it. The audited results have zero axiom dependencies.
